newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FORECAST-No Czech rate cut Thursday -dealers.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-No Czech rate cut Thursday -dealers.

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB) is unlikely to cut interest rates when it holds its regular board meeting on Thursday afternoon, dealers polled by Reuters said.
The markets have been rife with speculation about an imminent rate cut since the government called for a relaxation of monetary policy last week.

But dealers said that recent comments from the central bank concerning the reasons for its original tightenening of monetary policy last summer and the current vulnerability of the crown made a cut this afternoon unlikely.

"My opinion is that they cannot cut... Now they changed the main reason for this tough monetary policy. Now they say they had to keep it because of the balance of payments. In other words they admit that they are on the defensive," said Petr Korous of Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka.

Last summer, the CNB raised the discount rate to 10.5 percent from 9.5 percent, the Lombard rate to 14 percent from 12.5 percent, and minimum reserve requirements to 11.5 percent from 8.5 percent. Two weeks ago reserve requirements were cut back to 9.5 percent.
At the time, the central bank said the moves were designed to cut inflation and slow growth in the money supply.
But inflation has fallen to under seven percent from around nine percent a year ago and M2 money grew at 7.1 percent in January compared with 17.8 percent in the same month last year.

With the CNB having apparently succeeded in its aims, many dealers and analysts expected a rate cut would be a logical move, especially in view of the sharp slowdown in economic growth. Last week the government halved its original 1997 growth forecast to a maximum of 2.7 percent.

However, on Tuesday CNB governor Josef Tosovsky identified the main economic problem as the current account deficit, not inflation, which reached 8.6 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) last year.
The deficit, one of the largest in the world relative to GDP, is covered by large capital inflows attracted by the country's wide interest rate differential with western countries.
Tosovsky also firmly rejected government criticism of the CNB's restrictive monetary policy, saying the central bank was not responsible for the slowdown in growth.
In such circumstances most dealers questioned by Reuters said an immediate cut in interest rates was very unlikely.
"The first interest rate cut in four years is always a really difficult decision...so I think they are going to wait," said one senior trader.

Ahead of the CNB board meeting the crown was trading slightly down on late Wednesday levels at 30.5 to the dollar and 17.7 to the mark implying a deviation from the mid-point of the crown's mark/dollar fixing basket of around minus 1.6 percent.
